gaps: G1: sections.lookup returns IDs not text — the proposed canvas-read API fallback was impossible.
G2: read reachability was conflated with write authority — a shared-in canvas could receive an update handle (confused deputy).
G3: canvases.create without channel_id yields an inaccessible (and free-team-impossible) canvas; permalink is not in the create response.
G4: snippet path ignored the 1 MB snippet_type contract and could consume a durable delivery on provider failure.
G5: IPC canvas payloads had no host-side byte/shape bounds; canvases.edit allows one change per call.

G6: quick-fix details dropped provider data (Discord embed author/footer/media text; Telegram venue address) and embed folding could bypass router budgets; free-team one-canvas-tab and edit-lock errors unhandled; shared-canvas read handles lacked provenance.
contradictions: C1: the plan claimed concurrent-edit safety via provider errors, but canvases.edit has no revision/CAS parameter — the guarantee was unsupportable.
resolutions: G1: export spike is a hard gate; READ drops from scope if the file-export path fails (no API alternative exists) — recorded as a deviation if hit.
G2: separate READ and WRITE capability sets; write handles minted only from the channel's bound canvas and agent-created canvases in this conversation.
G3: create passes the host-derived channel_id, surfaces the permalink via files.info with a non-fatal failure path; free-team tab-exists returns the existing bound canvas.
G4: UTF-8 byte size chooses the vehicle before any upload (snippet ≤1MB, .txt above); ANY provider failure falls back to the existing split/truncate text path so delivery is never lost.
G5: strict host-side bounds (markdown ≤150KB, title ≤300, one op per call, enum allowlist, strict schemas) enforced at IPC before provider calls.

G6: embed folding covers all human-readable fields under per-embed UTF-8 caps AND the router aggregate budget; venue address included; free-team and lock errors have explicit fixture-tested behavior; shared-canvas read handles mint only from conversation-bound file_share events, never files.list.

C1: replaced with honest last-write-wins semantics, host-side per-canvas serialization of our own ops, destructive replace gated behind fresh lookup, human-edit races documented in the tool description.
summary: CONTENT-1 plan grilled via four Codex critique rounds (18 findings: 6/4/4/4, P1s extinct by round 3); every finding folded into the plan text; scope locked by Ravi (six quick fixes + Slack canvas; Teams deferred to TEAMS-1; reactions/edits backlog).
